ENGLISH LANGUAGE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #9
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which article goes before 'uniform'? (1 mark)
   A. one
   B. an
   C. the
   D. a

2. If you make a small mistake on a form, you should (1 mark)
   A. tear the page
   B. scribble over it
   C. draw one neat line through it and write the correct word
   D. leave it

3. Which word has the same vowel sound as 'bird'? (1 mark)
   A. time
   B. toy
   C. turn
   D. card

4. Which word has both the sounds /ɔɪ/ and /l/? (1 mark)
   A. road
   B. oil
   C. toy
   D. boy

5. 'Practice makes perfect' teaches us that (1 mark)
   A. the more we practise, the better we become
   B. practice is a waste of time
   C. perfect people never practise
   D. we should never try

6. 'As busy as a bee' means (1 mark)
   A. very tall
   B. very busy
   C. very quiet
   D. very lazy

7. What does 'proofread' mean? (1 mark)
   A. Read your work carefully and correct mistakes
   B. Copy from a book
   C. Write faster
   D. Draw pictures

8. Which is the best way to end a story? (1 mark)
   A. With a feeling or a lesson
   B. With the word 'the'
   C. With a list of numbers
   D. With nothing

9. Which word has the vowel /eɪ/? (1 mark)
   A. pen
   B. wet
   C. wait
   D. bed

10. Which letter is a tail letter? (1 mark)
   A. o
   B. t
   C. g
   D. m

11. An antiseptic is (1 mark)
   A. a strip of cloth
   B. a liquid or cream that kills germs on a wound
   C. a kind of bicycle
   D. a road sign

12. In which direction does the sun set? (1 mark)
   A. South
   B. West
   C. East
   D. North

13. A comic is a story told in (1 mark)
   A. a series of small pictures
   B. a table
   C. a single long word
   D. a mathematical sum

14. Which is an object pronoun? (1 mark)
   A. him
   B. his
   C. I
   D. he

15. Which word has the short sound /ʊ/? (1 mark)
   A. cook
   B. moon
   C. fruit
   D. spoon

16. Listening and diet: Which sentence is correct? (1 mark)
   A. I would like to be a nurse.
   B. I would likes to be a nurse.
   C. I would like to being a nurse.
   D. I would like be a nurse.

17. What is the superlative of 'good'? (1 mark)
   A. most good
   B. best
   C. goodest
   D. better

18. To reply to a message means to (1 mark)
   A. ignore it
   B. answer it
   C. delete it
   D. forward it only

19. Dialogues: Which question is inferential? (1 mark)
   A. Where do they see the reply?
   B. How do you think Baraka felt at the end?
   C. Who wrote the address?
   D. Which button did they click?

20. What does 'indigenous' mean? (1 mark)
   A. Damaged by pests
   B. Belonging naturally to a place
   C. Grown in a factory
   D. Very expensive

21. What should your voice do at the end of a question when reading aloud? (1 mark)
   A. Stop suddenly
   B. Fall to a whisper
   C. Rise
   D. Stay flat

22. Which sentence is a good ending for a story? (1 mark)
   A. We caught the goat together, and I was tired but proud.
   B. Then a goat.
   C. Farm.
   D. And the sun.

23. In which word is 'gh' silent? (1 mark)
   A. tough
   B. night
   C. enough
   D. cough

24. Which is a sign of good speaking fluency? (1 mark)
   A. Stopping after every word
   B. Speaking as fast as possible
   C. Speaking clearly at a steady pace
   D. Whispering so nobody hears

25. What does 'customer' mean? (1 mark)
   A. A person who sells goods
   B. A teacher
   C. A person who buys something or uses a service
   D. A doctor

26. Which word is an adverb of time? (1 mark)
   A. upstairs
   B. quietly
   C. yesterday
   D. here

27. Where does an adverb of frequency such as 'always' usually go in a sentence? (1 mark)
   A. Before the main verb
   B. Inside a word
   C. At the end after a full stop
   D. Before the capital letter

28. When is it fair to interrupt a speaker? (1 mark)
   A. When you did not hear or someone needs urgent help
   B. When you disagree loudly
   C. When you are bored
   D. When you want to talk instead

29. What is a factual text? (1 mark)
   A. A poem only
   B. A made-up story only
   C. A text that gives true information
   D. A joke

30. What does a smile usually show? (1 mark)
   A. Anger
   B. Fear
   C. Boredom
   D. Happiness or friendliness

31. Why should you not click on strange pop-up advertisements? (1 mark)
   A. They may be unsafe
   B. They improve your reading
   C. They are always free prizes
   D. They are required by the teacher

32. In a comic, what do speech bubbles show? (1 mark)
   A. The page number
   B. What the characters say
   C. The price
   D. The author's name

33. Which question word asks about a thing or an action? (1 mark)
   A. what
   B. whose
   C. when
   D. where

34. Which day is spelt correctly? (1 mark)
   A. Wednsday
   B. Wenesday
   C. Wensday
   D. Wednesday

35. Which is the correct spelling? (1 mark)
   A. neccessary
   B. necessary
   C. necesary
   D. necessery

36. Which word begins with the cluster 'pr'? (1 mark)
   A. protect
   B. brush
   C. clap
   D. grow

37. Which is a yes/no question? (1 mark)
   A. Is the compound clean?
   B. Where is the bin?
   C. Who is the captain?
   D. What did you sweep?

38. What does 'skimming' mean? (1 mark)
   A. Reading backwards
   B. Looking for one number
   C. Reading quickly to get the main idea
   D. Copying a passage

39. Which is a fact, not an opinion? (1 mark)
   A. Everyone should join.
   B. The club meets on Fridays.
   C. Saving is a good idea.
   D. The club is the best.

40. Which sentence has a preposition of direction? (1 mark)
   A. The book is on the desk.
   B. The cat is under the chair.
   C. The bank is near the school.
   D. The children walked along the road.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Change these adjectives into adverbs: gentle, angry, quick. (3 marks)

42. Give two differences between a friendly letter and an SMS. (2 marks)

43. Write two similes about food. (2 marks)

44. Write the -ing form of each verb: make, run, play, lie. (4 marks)

45. Read: 'Juma asked his mother to add vegetables to his lunch.' Say why Juma did this, using the story 'A Pot of Vegetables'. (2 marks)

46. Describe the five-finger test for choosing a book. (4 marks)

47. Explain the difference between 'good' and 'well'. Give one sentence for each. (4 marks)

48. Write the -ing form of: run, sit, swim. (3 marks)

49. Explain the difference between a common noun and a proper noun. Give one example of each. (3 marks)

50. Explain what the proverb 'Many hands make light work' means and give an example. (3 marks)

51. Explain why reading with expression is important. (2 marks)

52. State two things you can find in a dictionary entry. (2 marks)

53. Write a friendly letter of about five sentences to a friend in another school about new road safety words you learnt. (5 marks)

54. Write two minimal pairs for /p/ and /b/. (2 marks)

55. Explain why we say 'a university' but 'an umbrella'. (3 marks)

56. List two facts from the story about how HIV cannot spread. (2 marks)

57. Write two ways you can show a speaker that you are listening actively. (2 marks)

58. Give a situation in which 'Prevention is better than cure' applies. (2 marks)

59. Punctuate: 'mama may i go to the shop' (2 marks)

60. Fill in much or many: (a) How ___ eggs? (b) How ___ sugar? (2 marks)

61. What kind of person is Baraka? Give one reason from the story. (3 marks)

62. Explain what 'prevention' means and use it in a sentence. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #9 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — a
   Uniform starts with the consonant sound 'yoo'.

2. C — draw one neat line through it and write the correct word
   A neat single line keeps the form readable.

3. C — turn
   Bird and turn both have /ɜː/.

4. B — oil
   Oil has /ɔɪ/ followed by /l/.

5. A — the more we practise, the better we become
   Repeating a skill helps us improve.

6. B — very busy
   Bees always seem to be working, so it means very busy.

7. A — Read your work carefully and correct mistakes
   Proofreading is checking spelling, punctuation and meaning.

8. A — With a feeling or a lesson
   A good ending gives the reader a feeling or a message.

9. C — wait
   Wait has /eɪ/, but wet, pen and bed have /e/.

10. C — g
   G hangs below the line.

11. B — a liquid or cream that kills germs on a wound
   It cleans wounds by killing germs.

12. B — West
   The sun sets in the west.

13. A — a series of small pictures
   Comics use pictures, often with speech bubbles.

14. A — him
   Him is the object form of he.

15. A — cook
   Cook has /ʊ/.

16. A — I would like to be a nurse.
   The pattern is would like to be + noun phrase.

17. B — best
   Good, better, best.

18. B — answer it
   To reply is to answer.

19. B — How do you think Baraka felt at the end?
   You must work it out from clues.

20. B — Belonging naturally to a place
   Indigenous plants and animals are native to a place.

21. C — Rise
   A question ends with a rising voice.

22. A — We caught the goat together, and I was tired but proud.
   An ending tells how the story finishes and how people felt.

23. B — night
   In 'night' the gh is not pronounced.

24. C — Speaking clearly at a steady pace
   Fluent speech is clear and steady.

25. C — A person who buys something or uses a service
   A customer visits a shop or a barber.

26. C — yesterday
   'Yesterday' tells when.

27. A — Before the main verb
   For example: 'I always brush my teeth.'

28. A — When you did not hear or someone needs urgent help
   Only interrupt for good reasons, and do so politely.

29. C — A text that gives true information
   Factual texts share facts.

30. D — Happiness or friendliness
   A smile shows a friendly feeling.

31. A — They may be unsafe
   Strange links can be unsafe.

32. B — What the characters say
   Speech bubbles hold spoken words.

33. A — what
   'What' asks about things, ideas and actions.

34. D — Wednesday
   Wednesday is spelt Wed-nes-day.

35. B — necessary
   One c and two s's.

36. A — protect
   'Protect' begins with p and r.

37. A — Is the compound clean?
   It starts with a helping verb and can be answered yes or no.

38. C — Reading quickly to get the main idea
   Skimming gives the gist.

39. B — The club meets on Fridays.
   A fact can be checked.

40. D — The children walked along the road.
   'Along' shows movement.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: gently, angrily, quickly
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: A letter is longer and has five parts, but an SMS is short and has a receiver, a message and a sender. A letter is better for news and feelings.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each difference.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: The bread was as soft as a pillow. The juice was as sweet as honey.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: making, running, playing, lying
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct spelling.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: Mama Zuri told him vegetables give vitamins that protect the body from sickness, so he wanted to stay healthy.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for vitamins or protection and 1 mark for linking to Juma.

46. (4 marks)
   Answer: Open the book at a page and read it. Hold up a finger for every word you do not know. Five fingers means too hard; one to three fingers is a good fit.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for reading a page, 1 for counting unknown words with fingers, 1 for what five fingers means, 1 for what one to three fingers means.

47. (4 marks)
   Answer: 'Good' is an adjective and describes a noun: She is a good singer. 'Well' is an adverb and describes a verb: She sings well.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule and 1 mark for each sentence.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: running, sitting, swimming
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

49. (3 marks)
   Answer: A common noun is a general name such as 'town'. A proper noun is the special name of one person, place or thing, such as 'Kisumu', and begins with a capital letter.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 for both examples.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: It means a job is easier when many people help. For example, the whole class can sweep the compound quickly.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning, 1 for a suitable example, 1 for clear expression.

51. (2 marks)
   Answer: It shows the meaning and feeling of a text and makes listeners understand and enjoy it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for meaning/feeling, 1 mark for the effect on the listener.

52. (2 marks)
   Answer: Any two: spelling, meaning, part of speech, example sentence, pronunciation.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

53. (5 marks)
   Answer: A letter with address and date, Dear ..., a body that mentions words such as roundabout, foot bridge and railway crossing, a closing and a name.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for address and date, 1 for greeting, 1 for body content, 1 for closing and name, 1 for punctuation.

54. (2 marks)
   Answer: For example: pin, bin and pat, bat.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: Both start with the letter u, but university starts with the consonant sound 'yoo', so it takes a. Umbrella starts with a vowel sound, so it takes an. We choose by sound, not by letter.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each example and 1 mark for the sound rule.

56. (2 marks)
   Answer: It cannot spread by playing, shaking hands, sharing a plate or hugging.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct fact.

57. (2 marks)
   Answer: Look at the speaker and nod; keep still and quiet; say 'I see'.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

58. (2 marks)
   Answer: Washing hands before eating prevents illness, which is better than getting sick and needing medicine.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a situation and 1 for linking it to the proverb.

59. (2 marks)
   Answer: Mama, may I go to the shop?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for capitals and comma, 1 for the question mark.

60. (2 marks)
   Answer: (a) many (b) much
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

61. (3 marks)
   Answer: He is kind and brave. He went to talk to Omondi, explained the facts and invited him to play.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a quality and 2 for the evidence.

62. (3 marks)
   Answer: Prevention means acting so that something bad does not happen. For example: Washing hands is a way of prevention.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for the meaning, 1 for a sentence.
